---
title: 10 · Test and personalize
description: Check your finished game on purpose, make it your own, and save a version you can share.
---
import Checkpoint from '../../../components/Checkpoint.astro';

Your finished game builds its board, runs 30-second rounds, and answers both the mouse and the keyboard. Let someone else play it before you make your final commit.

## Try inputs on purpose

Testing means looking for the cases that break things, not only the ones that work. Try each row:

| Try this | What should happen |
| --- | --- |
| Press Start with an empty name box | The round starts, and the messages call you Player |
| Click MISAbot, then an empty hole | The score goes up once, and the miss counts toward accuracy |
| Press the key in MISAbot's hole, with Caps Lock on | The bop still counts |
| Hold a key down over MISAbot | Only one bop counts |
| Right-click the board | No menu opens, and nothing scores |
| Type `Mary Ann` in the name box | The space types normally, and no round starts |
| Press Space, then Escape | A round starts, then ends with your result |
| Let the timer reach 0 | MISAbot disappears, and Start works again |
| Press Start twice quickly | Only one round runs; the timer doesn't speed up |

To check the end-of-round message without playing a perfect round, expose the game to the console for a moment. Add this line at the end of `main.js`:

```js title="Temporary last line of workshop/main.js"
window.game = game;
```

Modules keep their variables private, so this deliberately makes `game` a global. Start a round, then type into the console:

```js title="Type in the browser console during a round"
game.score = 30;
game.stop();
```

The message should end with `Legendary bopper!`. Try scores of 15, 5, and 0 to see the other titles. Delete the `window.game` line afterward; it's only for testing.

## Make one change

Make the game yours. Pick one of these, change it, and play again:

- **Round length.** Change `ROUND_SECONDS` in `game.js`. A 15-second round makes a good warm-up.
- **Speed.** Change the numbers in `POP_DELAYS`. Smaller numbers mean less time to react.
- **Titles.** Rewrite the messages in `rank.js` so they sound like you and your friends.
- **Keys.** Change `KEYS` in `board.js`. A number pad works too: `["7", "8", "9", "4", "5", "6", "1", "2", "3"]`. Keep exactly nine keys, one per hole.
- **Colors.** Change `--teal` and `--teal-dark` at the top of `style.css`.

Avoid asking for details the game doesn't need, such as student numbers.

## Save the finished version

From `workshop`:

```bash
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Finish my Bop the Bot game"
```

`git add .` stages every changed file in the current folder, including the new modules. Check the `git status` list first, so you only commit files you mean to.

Trade laptops with a neighbor, or play each other's versions. Compare scores, and tell them what you changed. There's no score you're supposed to get.

If an edit breaks the game, open the console and read the first red line, including its file name and line number. The [troubleshooting page](../../help/) explains common errors. [Recovery checkpoints](../../checkpoints/) are there if you need a working reference while keeping your version safe.

When you're ready to share a link that anyone can play, follow [Put your game online](../../moving-forward/publishing/).
